what_its_for: Tocilizumab is used to treat several conditions where your immune system is overactive. These include rheumatoid arthritis (joint pain and swelling), giant cell arteritis (inflammation of blood vessels in the head), polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (types of arthritis in children), cytokine release syndrome (a serious immune reaction sometimes caused by cancer treatments), and COVID-19 in hospitalized patients who need oxygen support.
how_to_take: Tocilizumab comes in two forms: an injection you give yourself under the skin (subcutaneous) or an infusion given into a vein (intravenous) by a healthcare provider. If you are using the self-injection form, inject it into your stomach, thigh, or upper arm. Rotate injection sites and never inject into skin that is bruised, red, tender, or hard. Before injecting, let the prefilled syringe or autoinjector warm up to room temperature for about 30 minutes. Do not shake the medication. Clean the injection site with an alcohol wipe and let it dry before injecting.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, weight, and how well you respond to treatment. For rheumatoid arthritis self-injections, the usual adult dose is 162 mg injected once every week or once every two weeks. For intravenous infusions, dosing is usually every 4 weeks, but your doctor may adjust this. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of the self-injection form, inject it as soon as you remember — as long as your next scheduled dose is not too soon. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not inject two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss an intravenous infusion appointment, call your doctor or infusion center right away to reschedule.
storage: Store tocilizumab in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it, and keep it away from heat and direct light. If needed, the prefilled syringe or autoinjector can be kept at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 28 days, but throw it away after that even if there is still medication left. Always keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who have infections, colds, flu, or chickenpox, as tocilizumab weakens your immune system and makes it harder for your body to fight infections. Do not receive live vaccines (such as the flu nasal spray, MMR, chickenpox, or shingles vaccines) while taking tocilizumab without first talking to your doctor. Avoid grapefruit interactions are not a major concern with this medication, but always tell your doctor about all other medications, supplements, or herbal products you take. Do not stop taking the medication without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, cough, shortness of breath, burning when urinating, or a wound that does not heal; stomach pain or changes in bowel habits, which could be a sign of a hole in the stomach or intestines; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe tiredness; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat; new or worsening symptoms of nervous system problems such as numbness, tingling, or vision changes; or signs of a blood clot such as swelling, pain, or redness in a leg, or sudden chest pain.
when_it_works: Some people may start to feel improvement in joint pain and swelling within 2 to 4 weeks, but it may take 3 to 6 months to feel the full benefit of tocilizumab. It is important to keep taking your medication even if you do not notice improvement right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Tocilizumab may harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 months after your last dose. A pregnancy registry exists for women who take tocilizumab during pregnancy. Breastfeeding: It is not known if tocilizumab passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Tocilizumab is approved for certain types of juvenile arthritis in children 2 years and older and for cytokine release syndrome in children. Doses are based on body weight. Older adults: Older adults may have a higher risk of infections while taking tocilizumab. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or kidney problems, as your treatment plan may need to be adjusted.
